headword: {急|せ}いては{事|こと}を{仕損|しそん}じる
reading: せいてはことをしそんじる
gloss: haste makes waste; more haste, less speed

definitions.gloss: haste makes waste; rushing leads to mistakes
definitions.explanation: A proverb warning that acting too hastily causes errors and poor results. Patience and careful action produce better outcomes.

examples.japanese: {急|せ}いては{事|こと}を{仕損|しそん}じるよ。{落|お}ち{着|つ}いて。
{急|せ}いては{事|こと}を{仕損|しそん}じるというから、もう{少|すこ}し{時間|じかん}をかけよう。
examples.english: They say haste makes waste, so let's take a little more time.

examples.japanese: {焦|あせ}って{準備|じゅんび}したら{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}をした。{急|せ}いては{事|こと}を{仕損|しそん}じるとはこのことだ。
examples.english: I rushed to get ready and forgot something. This is exactly what they mean by haste makes waste.

notes:
A common Japanese proverb equivalent to the English "haste makes waste" or "more haste, less speed." The verb {仕損|しそん}じる means "to fail" or "to bungle," so the literal meaning is "if you rush, you will bungle the task."

COMMON PATTERNS:
The {急|せ}いて is the te-form of {急|せ}く (to hurry), and は adds contrastive emphasis: "if you hurry (in contrast to being patient), you will fail." The proverb is typically quoted in its full form.

SIMILAR PROVERBS:
- {急|いそ}がば{回|まわ}れ: if in a hurry, take the roundabout way — similar meaning emphasizing careful action
- {慌|あわ}てる{乞食|こじき}はもらいが{少|すく}ない: the beggar who panics gets less — similar admonition against rushing

USAGE:
Often used as gentle advice or self-reflection when someone has made a mistake due to rushing. Commonly followed by という, とはこのことだ, or だよ.
